World.title: President Cyril Ramaphosa mourns passing of rising sports stars
World.content:
Cyril Ramaphosa has sent his condolences after the death of Jayden Adams and Luqobo 'Bibo' Makwedini. Image: @FIFA website/ @ASBHOfficiel Image

The South African sports community was rocked this weekend after it came to light that two young sports stars had passed away in tragic circumstances.

Condolences have poured in after the body of Bafana Bafana and Mamelodi Sundowns midfielder Jayden Adams was found at a property in Cape Town.

The death of the 25-year-old footballer, who featured at the FIFA World Cup, has reverberated around the global football community.

A cause of death has not been officially revealed, but it is widely reported that Adams tragically took his own life.



Western Cape police spokesperson Captain FC van Wyk stated: “Cape Town Central police registered an inquest for investigation following the discovery of the body of a 25-year-old male on Saturday, 11 July 2026, at 11:06 at a premises in Military Road, Schotsche Kloof.”

Meanwhile, rising rugby star Luqobo ‘Bibo’ Makwedini has died at the age of 20 after collapsing following a training session with French club AS Béziers Hérault.

French media reports said Makwedini is believed to have suffered a cardiac arrest.



A product of Wynberg Boys’ High School in Cape Town, Makwedini moved to France last year after joining the Béziers academy ahead of the 2025/26 season.

President Cyril Ramaphosa sends condolences

President Cyril Ramaphosa has offered his deep condolences to the families of Jayden Adams and Luqobo Makwedini.

President Ramaphosa said: “It is particularly tragic that we are suffering the loss of two outstanding, young athletes at a time when our nation continues to immerse itself in the FIFA World Cup tournament, as well as the Springboks’ and Springbok Women’s matches against Scotland and the USA Eagles in Pretoria today.



“We are grateful for the joy and victories Jayden and Luqobo have given us and their teams as they lived their dreams and held South Africa’s name high on the scoreboards of global sport.”

Tributes pour in from far and wide

Béziers president, former Springbok captain Bob Skinstad, confirmed the devastating news of Makwedini’s passing in a statement on Friday evening.

“Luqobo joined our training centre during the off-season and quickly became a valued member of the Red and Blue family,” Skinstad said.



“His commitment, kindness, and personal qualities deeply impressed everyone at the club.

“Today, the entire Red and Blue family is united in mourning and deeply shaken by this heartbreaking loss.”

World.title: Jayden Adams’ mother: He kicked everything, even potatoes
World.content:
Jayden Adams: Just weeks before his death, the Bafana Bafana midfielder's parents reflected on the childhood memories and sacrifices that shaped his football journey. Image: Facebook/Bafana Bafana and Mamelodi Sundowns

Just weeks before his death, Jayden Adams’ parents gave South Africans a glimpse into the footballer’s life during a television interview.

Candice and Juanito Adams revealed the childhood memories, sacrifices and faith that shaped Jayden into one of the country’s brightest football talents.

The Bafana Bafana and Mamelodi Sundowns midfielder died on 11 July at the age of 25.



He kicked everything, even potatoes

In the interview, Candice shared that her son’s love for football started when he was just three years old.

“He kicked everything in the house,” she recalled with a smile. “Even the potatoes never lasted because he kicked them around.”

She said football quickly became part of his everyday life and that his passion for the game was impossible to miss.

Juanito said his son’s talent stood out from an early age.

“It was evident,” he said, recalling how Jayden’s natural ability became clear every time he stepped onto the field.

Prayer carried him through difficult times

Candice said the family relied on prayer during difficult moments in his football journey. She encouraged him to stay strong, shake off disappointment and keep pushing towards his dreams.



Watching him represent Bafana Bafana filled her with pride. “It brought tears of joy,” she said.

His father described Jayden as humble and respectful. Furthermore, Juanito said his son earned every success through years of sacrifice, discipline and hard work.

SAPS confirms inquest

Western Cape SAPS has opened an inquest after officers found the footballer’s body at a property in Schotsche Kloof, Cape Town, on Saturday. Spokesperson Captain FC van Wyk said police are investigating the circumstances surrounding his death.

Tributes have continued to pour in from across South Africa as teammates, clubs and supporters remember not only Adams’ talent but also the humility and character his parents said defined him throughout his life.

World.title: Who did Jayden Adams leave behind? Partner, child and more
World.content:
The sudden passing of 25-year-old South African footballer Jayden Adams has South Africans, and football fans across the world, in mourning. Beyond his achievements on the pitch, Adams was a devoted partner, father, and family man whose absence will be felt most at home. Here is a look at who Jayden Adams leaves behind.

WHO DOES JAYDEN ADAMS LEAVE BEHIND?

HIS PARTNER – AQUEELAH ADENDORF

Jayden shared his life with his longtime partner, Aqueelah Adendorf. Their relationship was marked by unwavering support and love. Aqueelah often described Jayden as her “best friend and greatest supporter,” and her tributes since his passing reveal the depth of their bond. She stood by him through the highs of his career, including his World Cup call‑up, and the challenges of balancing fame with family life.

Take a look at her heartfelt tribute to Jayden…

“There are no words to describe the pain I’m feeling. 💔. Rest in peace, my love. Thank you for every memory, every laugh, every hug, and every moment we shared. You were not only the love of my life but also my greatest supporter and my best friend,” she wrote.



“A part of my heart left with you, and I will carry your love with me forever. Until we meet again, I’ll miss you every single day. Rest easy, my angel. I love you always and forever. 🕊️❤️,” she continued.

DAUGTER: ALLAIA-JAYDA

In 2021, Jayden and Aqueelah welcomed their beautiful daughter, Allaia‑Jayda. Fatherhood was a big part of who Jayden was. He often shared tender moments with his child. Allaia‑Jayda is five years old. She has her own Instagram account with around 3400 followers.



FAMILY

Jayden’s family played a significant role in his journey, he was reportedly raised by his grandmother Marianna Adams. During the 2026 FIFA World Cup, he endured the tragic loss of his grandmother, yet continued to represent South Africa.

“My legs were playing, but my heart was in heaven with her,” he said reflecting on her death.



“He’s the reason I’m here… Wearing the green and gold meant everything to her,” he continued.

A COMMUNITY OF SUPPORT

Beyond his immediate family, Jayden also leaves behind a wider circle of teammates, friends, and supporters.

World.title: Transfer report: Kaizer Chiefs offer cash and players to buy Stellenbosch star
World.content:
Kaizer Chiefs have reportedly tabled an offer for highly-rated Stellenbosch FC winger Langelihle Phili. The 20-year-old winger enjoyed a breakout campaign last season, scoring seven goals and registering one assist.

The Soweto giants are not only looking to sign the talented attacker but are also prepared to offer several fringe players to Stellenbosch FC in an effort to complete the deal. Fernando Da Cruz is eager to bolster his attacking options before the new campaign gets underway.

LANGELIHLE PHILI TO KAIZER CHIEFS

According to SABC Sport journalist Mazola Molefe, Kaizer Chiefs have already made their move for the exciting youngster.



Speaking on SABC Sport, Molefe said: “I’ve got some breaking news regarding Kaizer Chiefs. There’s a lot happening inside that Naturena camp, and one of them is their interest in Langelihle Phili at Stellies.

“I can tell you 100% guaranteed fact that Kaizer Chiefs have indeed tabled an offer for the player. They’re trying to also move a couple of their fringe players over to Stellies as well, a bit of a swap deal.

Also read: Mngqithi:’Someone blocked my move to Kaizer Chiefs’

“The under-23 international has turned a lot of heads in recent times and Amakhosi are hell-bent on getting him on their books as part of coach Fernando Da Cruz’s new squad makeup.”

Born on 21 January 2005 in Tshelimnyama, Phili began his football journey in the AmaZulu FC academy before joining Stellenbosch FC, where he quickly established himself as one of South Africa’s brightest young talents.

The speedy winger announced himself in 2023 after winning both the Player of the Tournament and Striker of the Tournament awards at the Engen Champ of Champs. He also helped Stellenbosch FC‘s reserve side win the Engen Knockout Challenge, the DStv Diski Challenge and the Premier League Next Generation Cup.



IMPRESSED FOR CLUB AND COUNTRY

Steve Barker handed Phili his senior debut after the winger signed his first professional contract in September 2024. He made an immediate impact by scoring on his debut against Nsingizini Hotspurs in the CAF Confederation Cup preliminary round.

Meanwhile, his impressive displays earned him a call-up to the South Africa Under-20 side. He played a key role as Amajita lifted the 2025 U-20 CAF Africa Cup of Nations, securing qualification for the FIFA Under-20 World Cup in Chile.

With Kaizer Chiefs now willing to include players in the deal, negotiations could intensify as Amakhosi look to beat any competition for one of the Betway Premiership’s most exciting young attackers.

World.title: Carte Blanche coming up: July – Mayday!
World.content:
The Sunday, 12 July episode of Carte Blanche investigates a series of alarming aviation incidents that have raised fresh concerns about airline safety, transparency and accountability in South Africa.

The programme examines how a routine flight to Cape Town came within minutes of disaster and another aircraft encountered difficulties while approaching its destination, highlighting just two of four serious incidents recorded over the past few years.

As aviation experts question whether these events are isolated occurrences or signs of deeper systemic safety failures, the investigation explores concerns over airline decision-making, incident reporting and whether passenger safety is being compromised behind the scenes.

Credibility among South African viewers

World.title: Who was Jayden Adams? Five things to know about Bafana star
World.content:
Jayden Adams passed away at the age of 25. Images via Instagram @jaydenadams_23

South Africa, and football fans across the world, are mourning the death of Bafana Bafana midfielder Jayden Adams who passed away at just 25 years old on Saturday, 11 July.

Adams played as a midfielder for both Bafana Bafana and Mamelodi Sundowns.

He died just after returning from FIFA World Cup 2026.



Details not made public

Details surrounding his death has not yet been made public, although there has been some speculation that this could have been suicide.

Speaking on behalf of the Adams family, mentor Brendine Johnson described the devastating impact of the midfielder’s passing.

“At this moment, things are still raw. The family wouldn’t want to be contacted right now; they wouldn’t be able to answer anyone,” Johnson said.

“This passing has ripped everybody apart. Returning from the World Cup just now, and then getting such news… I had a close conversation with him on Thursday. The guy was really positive about returning after the World Cup and going forward.”

FIVE THINGS TO KNOW ABOUT JAYDEN ADAMS

Adams was the first player from Stellenbosch FC’s academy to sign a professional contract. His rise from local youth football to the senior squad inspired many young athletes in South Africa.

The soccer star played a pivotal role in Stellenbosch’s 2023 Carling Knockout Cup victory, showcasing his skill, composure, and leadership on the pitch.



In 2025, he joined Mamelodi Sundowns, where he quickly became a key midfielder. His contributions helped the team secure both the CAF Champions League and the Betway Premiership titles.

Adams represented Bafana Bafana at the 2026 FIFA World Cup, starting against Mexico and Czechia, and coming off the bench in the win over South Korea.

His resilience was remarkable, especially as he continued playing despite personal loss of his grandmother during the tournament.

Adams left behind a five-year-old daughter and partner Aqueelah Adendorf.

World.title: Conor McGregor loses in 69 seconds in latest UFC 329 flop
World.content:
Max Holloway lands a punch on Conor McGregor just seconds before the Irishman lost due to a right knee injury. Image: Ian Maule / AFP

Former double world champion Conor McGregor lost to Max Holloway after only 69 seconds because of a right knee injury on Saturday, in his return to the Ultimate Fighting Championship after a five-year layoff.

Referee Mike Beltran stopped the mixed martial arts welterweight contest at UFC 329 in Las Vegas after Ireland’s McGregor, 37, fell to the mat three times in the first minute.

READ | Dricus du Plessis ‘off to take care of business’ in next UFC bout



Hurt his right knee

McGregor jumped and launched a roundhouse kick at Holloway in the opening seconds, but hurt his right knee as he planted his foot.

He crumpled twice more and grabbed at his right knee, prompting Beltran to end the bout.

“What can I say? I had him weak in the knees I guess,” Holloway said.

“So much hype. We’ve got to run it back one more time,” he said. “For it to end like this sucks.”

McGregor walked out of the octagon without comment and Holloway hoped the Irishman’s injury was “not too crazy”.

Holloway said he knew his opponent was in trouble when he backed off.



“I could tell. His whole demeanor changed. He said, ‘Fight! Fight!’,” added Holloway

Most marketable star

In what Conor McGregor called “the comeback of all comebacks in sports history”, the bout was a rematch of a 2013 featherweight fight which the Irishman won by unanimous decision.

McGregor had not fought since breaking his left leg in a 2021 defeat to American Dustin Poirier.

McGregor had been the UFC’s most marketable star before that injury, in 2016 becoming the first to hold two titles simultaneously at different weights.

He reportedly earned more than $100 million for losing a boxing superfight against Floyd Mayweather in 2017.

McGregor’s last UFC victory was a 40-second triumph over American Donald Cerrone in January 2020.

Earlier, England’s Paddy Pimblett stopped France’s Benoit Saint Denis by submission after only 52 seconds of a lightweight bout.

Time for Conor McGregor to retire?

Let us know by clicking on the comment banner below …

World.title: SAHRC calls for alcohol law reform
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The SA Human Rights Commission has welcomed the inquest findings that several individuals failed to act to prevent the Enyobeni tragedy.

The Commission’s Eileen Carter is calling on government to expedite alcohol law reforms.

“The World Health Organization has pointed towards South Africa being amongst the top 10 consumers of alcoholic beverages, and it certainly leads to a scourge of incidences that are preventable.

“We also found in our report that from a systemic failures point of view, the Department of Trade and Industry and the Department of Social Development have failed to progress legislation that is designed from South Africa's policies to prevent and address these issues.

“So, for more than 10 years, the liquor amendment bill as well as the Control of Marketing of Alcoholic Beverages bill have just been lying dormant and it hasn't been properly progressing through the structures yet.

“Now, as a result of this inquest outcome as well, the Commission will now be calling for meetings with the relevant ministers so that we can see where the holdup is in progressing these pieces of legislation that speak to protecting the rights not only of the youngsters who tragically died in this incident, but South Africa as a whole,” Carter said.

On 26 June 2026, a total of 21 young people were killed at Enyobeni Tavern. The youngest victim was 13 years old.

World.title: All eyes on SA court as UK fugitive set to appear
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - South Africa is no haven for fugitives of justice.

That's the warning from authorities after Ndodana Tshuma, a British citizen, was arrested in Johannesburg on Friday.

He's wanted in the UK for the murder of his wife and two daughters.

All eyes will be on the Johannesburg Magistrate's Court, as he appears there on Monday.

His arrest in Kensington has set the stage for what is expected to be the start of extradition proceedings.

This Johannesburg suburb has become the focus of an international murder investigation.

His arrest followed an intelligence-led operation involving Interpol, Crime Intelligence and the Organised Crime Investigation Unit.

British authorities wanted Tshuma in connection with the murders of his wife, 42-year-old Nothabo Tshuma, and their daughters, Natalie and Nala, aged 15 and 5.

Their bodies were found at their home near Bedford in England.

Extradition proceedings are anticipated to begin as UK authorities seek his return to stand trial.

Police in South Africa have been applauded for Tshuma’s arrest.

Authorities said the arrest sends a clear message that South Africa will not become a haven for fugitives seeking to evade justice.

World.title: Apartheid Museum obituary installation on Mandela Day
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The Apartheid Museum and the Don Mattera Legacy Foundation will unveil the Don Mattera Obituary installation on Mandela Day.

The renowned poet and activist died on 18 July, 2022.

Teddy Mattera of the Don Mattera Legacy Foundation said this was a way to remember Mattera.

“His activism demonstrated very clearly the kind of commitment that he had made and so I think it's apt that the Apartheid Museum should take this time and look at how serendipitous it is that on this particular day, Mandela Day, we find Don Matera being celebrated and remembered at the Apartheid Museum.

“It really signifies the importance once again of an unsung hero who may have been sidelined either because of, you know, not belonging to the right political party at the time because a black consciousness person but all the same, you know, our heroes remain our heroes irrespective of what liberation camp they come from."

World.title: Argentina's Scaloni says England World Cup semi 'just a football game'
World.content:
ATLANTA - Argentina coach Lionel Scaloni insisted Wednesday's heavyweight World Cup semi-final against England was "just a football game" after his side beat Switzerland 3-1 in the last eight.

Alexis Mac Allister put the defending champions ahead early in Kansas City on Saturday but Dan Ndoye scored a deserved equaliser midway through the second half.

Disaster struck minutes later for Switzerland when Breel Embolo was shown a second yellow card for simulation, reducing them to 10 men.

Julian Alvarez broke Swiss hearts in the 112th minute before substitute Lautaro Martinez added a last-gasp third.

Argentina now turn their attention to the semi-final in Atlanta, which promises to be a tense encounter.

The history of matches between England and Argentina is peppered with flashpoints on the pitch, set against a lingering sovereignty dispute over the Falkland Islands, known in Spanish as the Malvinas, in the South Atlantic Ocean.

Britain sent a military task force in 1982 to reclaim the islands after Argentine troops invaded.

But Scaloni sought to put politics aside after Argentina's victory at Arrowhead Stadium.

"Look, this is a football game," he said. "OK, so the message is that this is a football game. That's what I can say.

"It is a football game and we will be playing against a very tough opponent. They have an excellent coach and this is a football game and that's all."

The game against England comes 40 years after a seismic encounter in the quarter-finals of the 1986 World Cup in Mexico.

Argentina secured a 2-1 victory at the Estadio Azteca with two goals from Diego Maradona, one the infamous "Hand of God" goal and the other a dazzling solo effort considered one of the best ever.

The teams have faced each other twice in World Cups since Argentina won on penalties in 1998, while England gained revenge four years later.

Scaloni admitted the defending champions would have to improve after another tough test following gruelling 3-2 wins over Cape Verde and Egypt.

"We won because of our ambition; we didn't want it to go to penalties," he said. "It was more about the desire to win than the quality of play."

He added: "We are in the semi-finals, a privileged position in football that we might take for granted, but it's not that easy.

"We have every reason to be happy, satisfied, and excited.

"Now we're going for everything we can, right to the end, with every last ounce of strength and every last drop of sweat.

"If we pull it off, great. If not, we're going to give it our all. Let there be no doubt about that."

World.title: In Sicily, drones at work to predict volcanic eruptions
World.content:
SICILY - Hovering over the volcano, a buzzing drone pauses in front of a laser beam on the crater's edge, as researchers test whether the devices can measure gases to predict eruptions.

On the Aeolian island of Vulcano, off the coast of Sicily, German researcher Marius Schaab, from the Technical University of Munich (TUM), stands next to a gas sensor mounted on a tripod, waiting for the drone his colleague has just launched to draw closer.

In this remote lunar landscape, where hot volcanic gases and steam smelling of sulphur rise eerily from the earth, the small propeller-driven device catches the eye.

The last eruption of the island's Grand Crater occurred in the late 19th century, but the volcano continues to show intense degassing activity -- to the awe of the visitors who are allowed to walk around the rim.

Soon, the drone positions itself along the axis of the sensor, which transmits an invisible laser beam that passes through the volcanic gas emissions before being reflected by the drone and travelling back.

The sensor works by "sending a laser beam through some gas and then onto some reflector that measures the intensity of the driving light", Schaab said,

The drone can move around and switch angles to take full measurements.

Using a laser allows the sensor to avoid the gas plume, the researcher told AFP.

World.title: Car crisis takes toll on Germany's young engineers
World.content:
FRANKFURT - Despite a year of searching, previous stints at big automotive suppliers and sending out about 50 applications, German software engineer Max Peil is still looking for a job.

Trained in computer vision, a critical part of autonomous and intelligent driving systems, Peil could once have expected to sail into a role at one of Germany's industrial giants.

But years of stagnant growth in Europe's biggest economy and increasingly fierce Chinese competition are now taking their toll on young engineers like Peil.

"Usually you just get rejected straight up," the 30-year-old told AFP in the western city of Frankfurt.

"I've had one interview. It was the same with my friends, one has sent over 60 applications."

- 'Golden age' is gone -

Known the world over for cutting-edge technology and innovative design, Germany's car industry, powered by exports, has so far managed to avoid the drastic decline seen in countries like Britain, France and Italy.

But Chinese carmakers like BYD and Xpeng have eaten into German carmakers' sales in the world's largest auto market, leading to painful adjustments at home.

World.title: Russian strikes kill six in Ukraine, officials say
World.content:
KYIV - Russia struck Ukraine with missiles, drones and guided bombs on Saturday, killing six people and wounding dozens of others, officials said.

Missiles also hit the capital, Kyiv, wounding 12 people, including two children, according to the city's mayor.

AFP journalists in Kyiv heard two series of explosions in the early hours, with an air alert siren sounding minutes after the first blast.

Moscow has been firing missiles and drones at Kyiv almost daily since launching its invasion in February 2022.

But a recent spate of deadly attacks using dozens of ultra-fast ballistic missiles has put Ukraine's air defence system under strain.

Russia launched more than 120 drones and 12 missiles during the night, half of them ballistic, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said in a post on X.

"Civilian infrastructure was hit even before the air raid alert was issued," he added.

He posted videos of emergency teams working in the smoke and rubble of ruined buildings.

Apartment buildings, offices and a theological school were damaged in Kyiv, while recovery efforts were underway in other regions, he added.

In the northern Ukrainian city of Sumy, "a guided aerial bomb" killed four people, including a young girl, the city's mayor, Artem Kobzar said.

A separate missile strike on the southern city of Odesa killed two others, regional governor Oleg Kiper said.

- Air defence call -

Zelensky said air defences "managed to shoot down most of the targets -- but not the ballistic ones".

He repeated his plea for allies to send more military aid to help it fight off the Russian invasion, now well into its fifth year.

World.title: Ramaphosa pays tribute to sports stars Jayden Adams and Luqobo Makwedini
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - President Cyril Ramaphosa has offered his deep condolences to the families of Jayden Adams and Luqobo Makwedini, who passed away at the ages of 25 and 20, respectively.

Adams, a Bafana Bafana and Mamelodi Sundowns midfielder, died just after he returned to South Africa from the FIFA World Cup.

Makwedini reportedly died in France following a practice session with his French club, AS Béziers Hérault.

“It is particularly tragic that we are suffering the loss of two outstanding young athletes at a time when our nation continues to immerse itself in the FIFA World Cup tournament, as well as the Springboks’ and Springbok Women’s matches against Scotland and the USA Eagles in Pretoria today.

“We are grateful for the joy and victories Jayden and Luqobo have given us and their teams as they lived their dreams and held South Africa’s name high on the scoreboards of global sport. May their souls rest in peace,” Ramaphosa said.

World.title: Day of mayhem: Violence and gunfire shake Ol Kalou by-election
World.content:
‎Residents protest along the Gilgil–Ol Kalou road at Chokereria after masked, armed men fired shots into the air and assaulted locals following an incident involving a DCP campaign vehicle. [Kipsang Joseph, Standard]

As campaigns ahead of the July 16 Ol Kalou parliamentary by-election draw closer to their end; fresh allegations of violence, intimidation, and voter bribery continue to be reported.

Masked gunmen traveling in vehicles with concealed and missing registration plates attacked a Democracy for Citizens Party (DCP) campaign vehicle at Pembroke Bridge along the Gilgil–Ol Kalou road yesterday.

World.title: Why Linda Mwananchi leaders cancelled Ol Kalou tour
World.content:
Linda Mwanachi leaders led by Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna held a series of rallies in Kisii County. [Linda Mwanachi, X]

Unity within the Opposition appears to be under fresh strain after the Edwin Sifuna-led Linda Mwananchi Movement cancelled plans to hold rallies in Ol Kalou Constituency this weekend.

The Linda Mwananchi brigade will instead convene a meeting in Nyahururu Town on Sunday. Analysts argue that the former deputy president probably thinks Kangata is attempting to popularise Sifuna in his Mt Kenya stronghold.

World.title: Karua condemns convoy attack, blames police lapse
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

PLP leader Martha Karua. [Boniface Okendo, Standard]

People's Liberation Party (PLP) leader Martha Karua has condemned an attack on her convoy at Gatoto Primary School in Mukuru kwa Reuben, alleging police failed to provide security despite a High Court order.

In a statement on Friday, July 10, Karua said she had accompanied members of the Gatoto Primary School Board of Directors to oversee the implementation of a High Court judgment restoring the school's management to its lawful board.

She alleged that the High Court had directed the Officer Commanding Station (OCS) at Mukuru kwa Reuben Police Station to provide security for the exercise.

According to Karua, when the board members reported to the station, the OCS was unavailable while his deputy declined to deploy officers, saying only the OCS could authorise the deployment.

Karua said they proceeded to the school without a police escort, where they found the gates locked.

She claimed the situation turned chaotic shortly after members of the media arrived, with a group of people pelting vehicles belonging to board members with stones and forcing the convoy to leave the area.

Karua further alleged that one of the attackers smashed the rear windscreen of her vehicle using a rungu.

Condemning the incident, Martha Karua said it raised broader concerns about respect for court orders and the rule of law.

"Today's events are not merely about Gatoto Primary School. They raise a broader national question about whether Kenyans can continue to rely on public institutions to enforce court decisions impartially and protect those exercising their constitutional rights," she said.

Karua called for investigations into both the attack and the alleged failure by police to enforce the court order, urging authorities to hold those responsible accountable.

World.title: Registrar of Political Parties okays Sifuna's removal as ODM secretary general
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna. [File, Standard]

The removal of Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna as the Orange Democratic Movement (ODM) Secretary-General has been formalised by the Office of the Registrar of Political Parties (ORPP).

In a letter, the registrar's office said that Sifuna’s removal process by the party’s National Executive Council complied with its constitution and the Political Parties Act.

"Upon review of the documents submitted by the party and the lack of response from Hon. Edwin Watenya Sifuna, we note that the removal of the party Secretary-General was in line with the Political Parties Act, Cap. 7D, and the ODM party constitution," the letter signed by ORPP Chief Executive Offier John Lorionokou reads.

He added that the office made the decision after considering communication on the ODM’s NEC powers to set up and determine issues of discipline within the party.

“The office has effected the change and updated the party records.”

Sifuna through his legal team challenged the ORPP decision.

In a letter, Senior Counsel Isaac Okero said that the move was a clear procedural irregularity and the changes should not be effected.

"Our client considers this action to be procedurally improper. Effecting changes to the party records violates the Political Parties Act, and our client will not hesitate to pursue the appropriate legal remedies," the letter by Okero says.

The battle for the SG’s post began on February 11, 2026, when an NEC meeting convened in Mombasa, passed a resolution to oust Sifuna replacing him with Busia Woman Representative Catherine Omanyo in acting capacity.

The Mombasa meeting was led by the then acting Party leader and Siaya Senator Oburu Odinga and other top leaders of the party.

Sifuna challenged his removal at the ODM party Disciplinary Committee and the Political Parties Disputes Tribunal.

At the ODM Disciplinary Committee Sifuna did not file a response to several allegations levelled against him which included contradicting the party’s position.

World.title: Kalonzo condemns police over their conduct during Saba Saba Day
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Police keep vigil as motorists are diverted along barricaded Parliament road, Nairobi during the Saba Saba Day commemorations on July 7,2026. [Elvis Ogina,Standard]

Wiper Patriotic Front Party Leader Kalonzo Musyoka condemned the National Police Service for turning its guns and batons on the citizens it exists to protect during the 36th Saba Saba Day.

Kalonzo said that Peaceful marchers were met with an excessive deployment of police officers, roadblocks and the deliberate closure of major roads, effectively curtailing the constitutional freedoms of movement, assembly and peaceful protest.

The Wiper Party Leader raised concerns that Plainclothes and masked officers forcibly seized young Kenyans from our streets into unmarked vehicles across the country while concealing their identities in blatant disregard of the rule of law and existing court orders.

“This is not policing, this is intimidation in service of a regime that fears its own people, even more disturbing is the growing pattern of police officers appearing to act alongside or provide protection to organised criminal gangs and militia groups that have terrorised innocent Kenyans in broad daylight,” said Kalonzo.

He pointed out that during the attacks on the Linda Mwananchi team in Kisii, at a hotel in Westlands, Nairobi and along Thika Road citizens were robbed and assaulted while law enforcement officers either stood by or failed to intervene such conduct gravely undermines public confidence in the National Police Service and has no place in a constitutional democracy.

Kalonzo reminded the National Police Service of its own motto: "Utumishi Kwa Wote — Service to All.” Not service to an individual or a political administration, but service to Kenya, to her Constitution, and to every Kenyan who calls this country home.

“Ask yourselves whose interests you defend when you arrest a mother marching for her missing son, or fire teargas at a student demanding accountability, I equally condemn the escalating attacks on opposition leaders, independent media and dissenting voices.

He said that the return of political intolerance under the Ruto regime is a dangerous attempt to drag Kenya back to the dark days of dictatorship that Saba Saba sought to end, a nation cannot claim to be democratic while intimidating political competitors, silencing the press and criminalising peaceful dissent.

Kalonzo said that these actions offend both the letter and the spirit of our Constitution calling for the immediate and unconditional release of every Kenyan arrested today while peacefully exercising their constitutional right to demonstrate.

“Peaceful protest is not a crime. It is a right expressly guaranteed under Article 37 of the Constitution, and no Kenyan should be detained for exercising that right, I also demand for immediate disciplinary action against all security agencies for their actions or inaction that has led to the violation of Kenyans constitutional rights,” said Kalonzo.

He said that when they form the next Government after the August 10, 2027 General Elections, we will deliver comprehensive police reform they will ensure every abduction and every death in custody is independently investigated and those responsible held fully accountable.

Kalonzo said when they get to power they will end the use of unmarked vehicles and unidentified officers against civilians and build a Police Service that answers to the Constitution, not to political power.

World.title: Kenya Kwanza leaders tell Uhuru to stay out of politics, act like a statesman
World.content:
Bungoma Governor Kenneth Lusaka addresses residents during the Kimilili Women and Youth Economic Empowerment Forum at St John's Miruri Primary School on July 5, 2026. [Jackline Inyanji, Standard]

Kenya Kwanza leaders led by Bungoma Governor Kenneth Lusaka, President’s aide Farouk Kibet and Taveta MP John Bwire, have called on former President Uhuru Kenyatta to uphold the dignity of the office he served and act like a statesman.

They hit out at the Linda Mwananchi leaders who attended the funeral of the brother of Bumula MP Jack Wamboka, claiming that the group is being used by former President Kenyatta.

World.title: Egypt secures new ways to book Grand Egyptian Museum tickets
World.content:
The Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities announced Saturday that the official website of the Grand Egyptian Museum (GEM) has been integrated into the applications of various mobile phone service providers operating in Egypt.

In a statement, the ministry explained that this step aims to facilitate online ticket booking and enhance secure access to the museum’s digital services.

The ministry indicated that this step will allow millions of users direct and secure access to the official website and enable them to book visits through a reliable and trusted channel.

It added that the museum’s official website is now available through the Vodafone app, the museum’s official technology sponsor, as well as the apps of Orange, Etisalat, and WE (a subsidiary of Telecom Egypt).

The ministry confirmed that this step comes under a cooperation framework between the GEM and mobile network operators in Egypt to enhance the visitor experience, raise cybersecurity levels, and protect the public from getting scammed by fake websites.

The ministry added that it is currently studying the possibility of enabling payment for visit tickets through mobile network wallets, in addition to the existing payment methods using bank cards.

This will provide easier and more flexible digital payment options and simplify the online booking process.

Commitment to integration

Minister of Tourism and Antiquities Sherif Fathy said that the initiative reflects the ministry’s commitment to strengthening integration between state institutions and the private sector to provide secure and reliable digital services.

This ensures easy access for visitors to official channels and enhances trust in electronic services.

He added that cooperation with mobile phone companies, given their extensive user bases and advanced digital platforms, contributes to expanding secure access to the GEM’s official website.

Fathy affirmed the ministry’s continued support for initiatives that utilize technology to develop tourism services and protect user data.

Digital strategy

The CEO of the GEM Authority, Ahmed Ghoneim, explained that this step is part of the museum’s strategy to build an integrated digital system that prioritizes visitor safety and ease of access to services.

He stated that making the official website available through mobile operators’ applications represents an additional, reliable channel for booking visits and obtaining official information.

Ghoneim stressed that the museum’s official website remains the only official channel for booking visits and accessing all museum-related information, urging the public to exercise caution and avoid dealing with unofficial websites or links from unknown sources.

World.title: Egypt faces intense heatwave across next 72 hours
World.content:
The Egyptian Meteorological Authority (EMA) forecasts a heatwave across the country for three consecutive days, with the country experiencing 72 hours of intense heat and high humidity starting Sunday.

Very hot and humid conditions will persist during the day across most of the country, with hot and humid weather along the northern coast.

Nights and early mornings will be slightly hot and humid.

Temperatures

According to the EMA, maximum temperatures in Greater Cairo and Lower Egypt will reach 36C until midweek, then drop to 35C on Wednesday and Thursday.

Maximum temperatures along the northern coast will range between 30-31C, reaching 37-38C in Upper Egypt, and up to 41C in southern Upper Egypt.

The high humidity will make temperatures feel two to four degrees Celsius higher than those recorded in the shade.

Fog and wind

Weather maps warn of fog formation between four AM and eight AM on some roads leading to and from northern Egypt, Greater Cairo, the Suez Canal cities, central Sinai, and northern Upper Egypt.

Drivers are advised to exercise caution, especially during the early morning hours.

Satellite imagery indicated intermittent wind activity across most of the country throughout the week.

The EMA urged citizens to follow weather forecasts regularly, avoid direct sun exposure during peak hours, and drink plenty of water and fluids.

Edited translation from Al-Masry Al-Youm

World.title: King Charles hosted Harry and Meghan for a private family gathering in Gloucestershire
World.content:
London —

King Charles and Queen Camilla hosted the Duke and Duchess of Sussex, Prince Archie and Princess Lilibet on Friday afternoon at Highgrove House, the king’s private country residence in Gloucestershire, England.

The meeting marks the first time King Charles has seen the whole family in four years, when Harry, Meghan and their children were in the UK for the late Queen Elizabeth’s Platinum Jubilee celebrations.

In the years since, Harry has made several quick trips back to the UK, most notably attending his grandmother’s funeral in 2022 and his father’s coronation in 2023. The last known meeting between the duke and his father was in September when the pair had tea at Clarence House in London.

A general view of the gardens at Highgrove House on June 5, 2013 in Tetbury, England. Chris Jackson/Getty Images

Harry, who arrived in the United Kingdom on Monday evening, returned this time to mark the one-year countdown to the Invictus Games, the Paralympic-style sporting competition for injured servicemen and veterans he set up more than a decade ago, as well as carry out several other charity engagements.

CNN previously reported that his wife and their two children might join him later in the week, as there was hope that the trip would allow King Charles to reunite with his young grandchildren, who are now 7 and 5-years-old.

The royal family will not release any images or further details of the meeting given that it was a private family occasion, CNN understands.

British media have reported that Meghan and the children were vacationing in Portugal, where they have a home, prior to visiting the UK this week.

CNN’s Anna Stewart and Lauren Kent contributed to this report.

World.title: Two killed in mass shooting at Canada’s largest Latin street festival in Toronto, police say
World.content:
Two people were killed and several others injured after at least two shooters exchanged gunfire amid crowds of roughly 13,000 people at Canada’s biggest Latin street festival in Toronto on Saturday, police said.

A total of six people were shot, and several suspects are believed to be at large after the shooting at the Salsa on St. Clair festival, Toronto Police Service Deputy Chief Frank Barredo said at a news conference late Saturday.

Both of the deceased victims were men, Barredo said, while the four injured victims were taken to hospitals with “serious injuries.” Investigators have cordoned off three crime scenes and recovered two firearms, but there is no ongoing threat to the public, he added.

“This seemed to be an exchange of gunfire between two individuals targeting each other,” Barredo said, adding the shooting “indiscriminately put vast numbers of people in danger.”

Festivalgoers ran down sidewalks from the scene, restricted by yellow tape, as scores of black police SUVs and patrol cars, heavy-duty armored vehicles and ambulances sped toward it, CTV footage showed.

Joanna Lavoie, a journalist with Canadian media outlet CP24 who was attending the festival, said “the mood instantly changed” after the gunshots rang out. Lavoie told CP24, a CNN affiliate, she saw a woman who appeared to have been shot and suffering from significant injuries.

“Everyone was just in disbelief and fear. It was a terrifying situation. We’re here to have fun … we didn’t expect anything like this to happen, and it was the last thing we expected.” Lavoie said.

Valerie Rodriguez told the Associated Press she was sitting outside a restaurant when she heard screams and saw people running. “A bunch of people … told us to lay down onto the floor,” she said.

Police work to disperse the crowds at the Salsa on St. Clair festival in Toronto, Canada. Courtesy CTV News A large police presence is at the scene at the Salsa on St. Clair festival in Toronto, Canada. Courtesy CTV News

Police said they secured the scene roughly an hour after the shooting began but continued to urge people to stay away from the area in the city’s midtown, where the multiday festival celebrating Latin culture has been held annually for 22 years, according to organizers.

Toronto Mayor Olivia Chow condemned the shooting as “a reckless, despicable act of violence at a crowded festival” and promised authorities would work tirelessly to identify the suspects.

“I will ensure Toronto Police have every resource they need to find those responsible, and they will keep working around the clock to get guns off our streets,” the mayor said in a statement on X.

Chow and police are urging any festival attendees with footage or information to contact police.

Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said in a statement he is “horrified” by the deadly shooting at the busy Toronto festival. “My prayers are with the families grieving their loved ones … and everyone who has been affected by this horrific event,” Carney wrote.

While deadly gun violence is less common in Canada than in the US, it still ravages communities.

Less than three weeks ago, the country was devastated by another mass shooting when a gunman opened fire in Montreal. A subsequent shootout with police killed two people in broad daylight and marked the first time a Montreal officer has been killed in the line of duty in two decades.

The shooting took place in a country with far stronger gun laws compared to the US and where mass shootings are infrequent. After Canada suffered its most deadly shooting in Nova Scotia in 2020, where 22 people were killed, the government put in place major reforms and bans on assault-style weapons.

This story has been updated with additional information.

World.title: Iran launched strikes on US military targets across the Gulf, Iran state media reports
World.content:
Iran targeted several US military sites across the Gulf early Sunday, Iranian state media reported, following the latest round of attacks launched by the US.

Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) launched ballistic missiles at the Al Udeid Air Base in Qatar, according to Iranian state broadcaster IRIB.

The IRGC also carried out what it said was a “heavy and surprise attack against logistics support facilities for naval vessels and refueling platforms used by US aircraft carriers at the Port of Duqm in Oman,” according to IRIB.

In Kuwait, Iran’s army said it had launched loitering drones against US military assets, including a Patriot air defense system. And in Bahrain, home to the US 5th Fleet, Iran’s army claimed it targeted a communications system and a radar installation belonging to US forces.

CNN was unable to verify the claims of attacks on US military sites. CNN has reached out to US Central Command.

Qatar and Kuwait both reported intercepting aerial attacks early Sunday local time. In Bahrain, sirens sounded and officials warned residents to proceed to the nearest safe location.

In Jordan, the IRGC claimed it destroyed military infrastructure including drone storage hangars at the Prince Hassan Air Base, Iranian media said.

CNN’s Eyad Kourdi contributed to this report.

World.title: Source: Oman proposes deal for Strait of Hormuz shipping routes
World.content:
Oman has drafted a proposal to manage traffic in the Strait of Hormuz through two separately controlled routes, a source with knowledge of the talks told CNN.

Under the agreement, which is yet to be finalized, both corridors would remain open. The Southern Corridor, through Omani territorial waters, would allow free navigation under pre-war conditions.

Vessels transiting the Northern Corridor, through Iranian territorial waters, would require prior approval from Iran, although no tolls would be imposed under the deal.

Iran’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi met with his Omani counterpart, Sayyid Badr Albusaidi, in Muscat on Saturday, during which both officials discussed mechanisms to ensure the safe passage of vessels in the waterway.

World.title: US citizen working in DR Congo tests positive for Ebola
World.content:
A US citizen working for a humanitarian group in the Democratic Republic of Congo has tested positive for the Bundibugyo strain of the Ebola virus, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention said in a statement on Friday.

The CDC said it is working with the patient’s employing organization, other federal agencies and partners in the DRC to help prevent further transmission and identify high-risk contacts.

No other details have been released about the patient. CNN has reached out to the CDC and the State Department for comment.

The number of confirmed Ebola cases in the DRC has increased to 1,830 including 648 deaths, government data showed late on Friday, Reuters reported.

No Ebola cases have been confirmed in the United States and “the overall risk to the American public and travelers remains low,” according to the latest data published Saturday on the CDC website. The outbreak remains confined to remote areas of the DRC and neighboring Uganda, and the risk of it spreading to the US is “considered very low,” it said.

Red Cross workers gather as aid agencies intensify efforts to contain the Ebola outbreak caused by the Bundibugyo virus in Democratic Republic of Congo, in June 2026. Gradel Muyisa Mumbere/Reuters

In May, the international charity Serge reported that an American Christian missionary physician – Dr. Peter Stafford – had “tested positive” after “presenting symptoms consistent with the virus.”

His wife, Dr. Rebekah Stafford and another physician, who were treating patients in the DRC when the outbreak began, as well as the Staffords’ four children – all aged under seven – were monitored for signs of the virus, the charity said.

The family, who had been living in DRC since 2021, was evacuated to Berlin, Germany, where Stafford was quarantined and treated in hospital.

Dr. Peter Stafford (left) contracted Ebola in May while living and working in the Democratic Republic of Congo with his wife Dr. Rebekah Stafford (right) and their four children. The family were evacuated to Germany where he was treated in hospital. Courtesy Serge

“That was a difficult time,” he said in an exclusive CNN interview after his recovery. “I had a high fever, I had weakness, at times too difficult even to walk on my own.”

Rebekah Stafford recalled feeling overwhelmed as she watched global efforts mobilize to help her husband, also aware that their Congolese friends wouldn’t receive the same level of care.

Despite their ordeal, she said their children are “doing really well.”

“Our oldest son definitely understood, telling our kids ‘hey guys, your dad has Ebola,’” she said, recalling having to explain that they couldn’t touch him, go in his room or be sure he would recover.

Last month, the first case of Ebola outside Africa was reported during the second largest outbreak on record in the DRC.

The patient, also a humanitarian worker, tested positive in France after returning home from a mission in the DRC, the French Health Ministry said.

This was the first reported case in France.

World.title: Iran’s supreme leader touts “historic” presence at late father’s funeral
World.content:
Iran’s supreme leader, Mojtaba Khamenei, thanked what he described as the “tens of millions” of people he said attended recent funeral ceremonies for his father, the late Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, in a purported message released by Iranian media today.

There were no signs that Mojtaba attended the days-long funeral events after significant speculation about his whereabouts and health.

“On this occasion, I sincerely thank the tens of millions of people whose astonishing, enemy-defeating and historic presence filled the cities and villages of Iran and Iraq, especially Tehran, Qom, Najaf, Karbala and Mashhad,” Iran’s semi-official Tasnim news agency cited Mojtaba as saying.

Khamenei’s funeral events were crowded with millions of mourners, but with a population of around 90 million, many others in Iran did not take part, and some were even angry at the spectacle.

Over several days of mourning, Iran’s Health Ministry said around 15 million people were expected to take part, but they did not reveal how that figure was calculated. CNN cannot independently verify how many people attended.

Mojtaba has not been seen in public since the war began in February, only communicating with his supporters via written statements attributed to him.

World.title: Copper Princesses 90 minutes from World Cup
World.content:
Zambia is on the verge of qualifying for the 2026 FIFA Under-17 Women’s World Cup as the Copper Princesses face Ethiopia on Sunday in the decisive return leg of the final round.

The match is scheduled for 15h00 local time in Addis Ababa, 14h00 Zambian time, at the Abebe Bikila Stadium.

Zambia take a 2-1 advantage into the tie after the first leg played at Levy Mwanawasa Stadium in Ndola a week ago.

The Copper Princesses will be seeking a historic third consecutive appearance at the global showpiece to be hosted by Morocco later this year.

Assistant Coach Naomi Phiri said the team is in Addis Ababa to finish the job.

“We are here to finish what we started back home. The girls understand what is at stake and we are ready,” Phiri said.

Zambia has featured in the last two editions of the FIFA Under-17 Women’s World Cup and will be banking on that experience.

A draw or win will see them through, but a loss by more than one goal would end their campaign.

World.title: Changala accuses Hichilema of “total arrogance” over campaign conduct
World.content:
Changala accuses Hichilema of “total arrogance” over campaign conduct

Civil rights activist Brebner Changala has accused President Hakainde Hichilema and the United Party for National Development (UPND) of taking Zambians for granted, saying the ruling party cannot expect to win support by returning to rural communities only during election campaigns after what he described as years of unresolved economic hardships.

Commenting on Hichilema’s campaign message to rural voters ahead of next month’s general election, Changala said the conduct of the ruling party during the campaign reflected what he described as growing arrogance towards the electorate.

“It’s clear that any mistake Zambians make to bring these guys back will be the last nail put in a coffin. All the UPND and Mr Hakainde want is votes. And that is total arrogance Zambians have been treated with,” he said.

Changala further accused the President of resorting to divisive politics after observing what he claimed was increasing public support for opposition parties during the campaign.

“Upon realising how Zambians are flocking to opposition rallies, Hichilema has resorted to divisive tribalistic campaigns. I want to warn Zambians that they must not vote for a man who is using tribe to cling to power. Mr Hichilema is using tribal politics and Zambians must be careful with him,” he said.

The activist argued that many citizens had endured difficult economic conditions during the UPND administration, citing the high cost of living, what he described as a shrinking democratic space and growing pressure on ordinary Zambians.

“In the last five years, Zambians have seen the worst, high cost of living, shrunk democratic space and stifled citizenry,” he said.

Turning to agriculture, Changala questioned the President’s recent pledge that farmers would receive immediate payments for maize deliveries through the Food Reserve Agency, saying previous delays had eroded confidence among producers.

“I wonder how the President thinks Zambians can still buy his claims on fertiliser and delayed payment to farmers under FRA when farmers have suffered for years due to delayed payments and poor planning by FRA,” he said.

He also challenged the ruling party’s messaging on free education, arguing that the policy should not be presented as an achievement unique to the current administration because Hichilema himself benefited from free education during his own schooling.

“Hichilema and UPND cannot claim credit for free education when the Head of State himself is a product of free education,” Changala said.

The activist further accused the government of interfering in opposition politics through what he described as the use of restrictive laws and alleged that the Patriotic Front had been taken over by individuals aligned with the state.

“He has stolen the country’s biggest opposition party, the Patriotic Front, and handed it to some state-sponsored individuals,” he said.

World.title: Mundubile Urges Public Institutions To Remain Neutral ahead of August polls
World.content:
NRPUP presidential candidate Brian Mundubile has appealed to public institutions to remain neutral and allow Zambians to decide freely in next month’s general election, warning that reports of partisan conduct by some institutions risk undermining public confidence in the electoral process.

In a statement issued at the weekend, Mundubile directed his appeal to civil servants, teachers, council workers and other public officers, saying their constitutional responsibility was to serve all citizens impartially regardless of which political party is in power.

“My appeal is straightforward: let every public institution remain neutral and allow the Zambian people to decide freely at the ballot box,” he said.

He assured civil servants across the country that an NRPUP government would respect their professionalism and protect them from political interference, stressing that public officers should carry out their duties without being influenced by partisan interests.

“You have a constitutional duty to remain professional, impartial and to serve all Zambians without political influence,” Mundubile said.

He said the National Reconciliation Party for Unity and Prosperity was committed to improving the welfare of civil servants, restoring professionalism in the public service and reducing political interference in government operations. He added that his administration would pursue reforms, including a debt swap arrangement aimed at strengthening local authorities and improving service delivery.

The opposition leader said the August 13 election should reflect the freely expressed will of the people rather than be influenced by fear, intimidation or the misuse of public institutions for partisan advantage.

Turning to his party’s campaign agenda, Mundubile said NRPUP remained focused on policies centred on job creation, support for farmers, youth empowerment, expanding opportunities in the mining sector, improving public services and building an economy that benefits all Zambians.

“Our campaign remains focused on practical solutions: creating jobs, supporting farmers, empowering young people, expanding opportunities in the mining sector, improving public services and building an economy that works for every Zambian. On 13 August, let us choose hope, unity and meaningful change,” he said before ending his remarks with a rallying call in Bemba.

His comments came as an editorial in one national newspaper urged civil servants to remain neutral and focus on their constitutional mandate of serving the public. The editorial cautioned that public officers who allow themselves to be drawn into partisan politics risk compromising their professional standing once elections are over and political leadership changes.

It argued that governments and politicians come and go, while the civil service remains a permanent institution that must continue serving citizens irrespective of the party in office.

Meanwhile, addressing supporters during a campaign rally in Chifunabuli over the weekend, Mundubile said his administration would govern the country based on Christian values, pledging to restore what he described as the principles enshrined in the Constitution.

“We want to govern this country using Christian values. To all Christian men and women, we assure you that we are going to restore this country. We are going to reset this nation so that we can exist again as a Christian nation,” he said.

He also promised to depoliticise and professionalise the civil service through a merit-based recruitment system, saying competent and qualified public officers would be protected regardless of political affiliation.

“We will start by depoliticising the civil service. We will start by professionalising the civil service. The civil servants who are competent and qualified will be protected. We will restore our democracy and values. We will uphold our principles and values enshrined in our Constitution,” he said.

Mundubile said reforming the civil service formed part of a broader programme to improve governance, arguing that policy changes alone would not succeed unless senior public positions were filled on merit rather than political loyalty.

“We believe that policy reforms are not enough without state professionals being appointed to top positions simply because they are cadres. This negatively impacts leadership and affects the people. We are going to reform the civil service, and as long as you are qualified, you should be very comfortable,” he said.

The NRPUP leader also pledged to improve conditions of service for teachers and other public workers by increasing housing allowances and expanding investment in the education sector. He said his government would build more classrooms to accommodate growing enrolment under free education, recruit more teachers and construct additional staff houses in phases.

“In terms of free education, while we focus on school-going children, we will not forget about our teachers. We love and appreciate all our teachers; without you, we wouldn’t be where we are today. As we support school-going children, we will also ensure that teachers are respected and valued. We plan to build houses for teachers in phases, increase the number of classrooms and improve housing allowances to help teachers access decent accommodation,” he said.

World.title: “Same Thieves” who have only changed their name – Hichilema
World.content:
President Hakainde Hichilema has told voters in Luangwa, Rufunsa and Chongwe not to “spoil” their votes on independent candidates, telling supporters that the ruling party needs five million votes to secure a stronger mandate than it won in 2021.

Addressing back-to-back rallies on Saturday, Hichilema described NRPUP leader Brian Mundubile and his running mate Makebi Zulu as figures from the former Patriotic Front who have simply regrouped under a new alliance name.

“Those who have come under new alliances, we know them. They have just changed their name. Do they become different? They are the same. The MP who was here is the same MP who was there in PF, now using a different party. They are the same crocodiles,” he said.

The Head of State urged supporters to vote with their heads rather than their stomachs, drawing a lengthy analogy between short-term hunger and long-term judgment.

“Vote using your brain, not using your stomach. The stomach feels hunger every day, but the head knows today, tomorrow, next month and next year. The stomach only knows that hour it is hungry, so when voting, use wisdom,” Hichilema said.

He said when a person is hungry they could even beat a child, but after eating they forget, while the head never forgets where a nation has come from. He referenced the debt burden Zambia inherited from the previous administration, asking supporters to weigh who was better between a leader who accumulated debt and one who worked to pay it back.

Turning to scripture, Hichilema likened returning to the former ruling party to the Israelites who, having been freed from slavery in Egypt by Moses, complained and longed to return.

“You have gone out of slavery and you are going to the promised land, then you want to go back to slavery? Can you go back? You go forward. On August 13, we are going forward,” he said.

The President also cautioned supporters against fielding or backing independent candidates, insisting that UPND was contesting a single candidate for each elective position in every constituency.

“I do not want anyone to go independent. There is only one position for UPND, that’s it. There is only one candidate for mayor, and one candidate for MP under UPND, and there is only one UPND symbol, the hand. Do not waste your vote on independents,” he said.

He questioned why he would field candidates under the UPND banner and then turn around to support independent contestants standing against them, asking supporters whether that would make sense.

Hichilema also dismissed suggestions that the opposition could win Lusaka, saying residents of the capital, together with those in Copperbelt, North-Western, Western and Central provinces, had already resolved to back the ruling party. He pointed to the turnout at a rally in Sinda the previous day as evidence of continued support, asking the crowd whether they had seen the numbers that gathered there.

On agriculture, the President said he wanted an end to farmers queuing for payment after delivering maize to the Food Reserve Agency, pledging that payments would instead be processed immediately through mobile money.

He also said he wanted to end situations where farmers shared limited Farmer Input Support Programme fertiliser and seed in tins or small measures, pledging to increase the number of FISP beneficiaries so that more farmers receive full allocations.

Hichilema further said the floor price for maize would be announced promptly once deliveries to the Food Reserve Agency begin, so that farmers are not left waiting.

Both Mundubile and Zulu had not responded directly to Hichilema’s “same thieves” characterisation by the time of publication. Campaigning continues this week as candidates make their final push across the provinces ahead of the August 13 general election.

World.title: ECZ Says Law Does Not Address Withdrawal of Running Mates Before Elections
World.content:
The Electoral Commission of Zambia (ECZ) says the country’s electoral laws do not provide for the withdrawal of a presidential running mate before a general election.

The matter has come into focus following the withdrawal of Organised People’s Party (OPP) running mate Andyford Banda and Citizens First running mate Moses Mawere, leaving presidential candidates Brian Mushimba and Harry Kalaba without running mates ahead of the August 13 General Election.

Speaking in an interview, ECZ Corporate Affairs Manager Patricia Luhanga said the resignation or withdrawal of a running mate does not invalidate a presidential candidate’s nomination or affect the electoral process.

Luhanga explained that while the law does not specifically address such a scenario, a presidential candidate remains validly nominated even after the withdrawal of a running mate.

She added that if such a candidate were elected President, a solution could be found after the election, including the appointment of another vice president in accordance with the law.

Meanwhile, ECZ Chairperson Mwangala Zaloumis said the Constitution only provides guidance on what happens if a Vice President vacates office after a presidential election and not when a running mate withdraws before polling day.

Zaloumis said the withdrawal of a running mate does not invalidate a presidential candidature because the law is silent on the matter.

She noted that the situation has exposed a gap in the country’s electoral legal framework, describing it as a legislative lacuna that may require future legal reforms.

World.title: HH assures Chongwe residents improved water supply
World.content:
President Hakainde Hichilema has assured residents of Chongwe district that the government is committed to improving water supply in the area as part of its continued efforts to enhance access to essential services.

Speaking during a community engagement in Chongwe, President Hichilema urged residents to vote for the United Party for National Development (UPND) in the August 13 elections, to enable the party to continue implementing development programmes across the country.

The President said the government has recorded significant achievements since assuming office, citing free education, increased Constituency Development Funds (CDF) allocations and expanded infrastructure development as some of the notable milestones.

“We are asking the people of Chongwe to support the UPND because of the massive development that Zambia has experienced under this administration, including the introduction of free education,” President Hichilema said.

He further urged Zambians to safeguard the peace and stability the country is currently enjoying, adding that the government remains committed to promoting unity and rejecting violence.

President Hichilema also advised voters against electing independent candidates, saying they may not effectively support the implementation of government programmes.

On agriculture, the President assured farmers that the Food Reserve Agency (FRA) would soon announce this year’s maize purchase price and that farmers will be paid promptly after delivering their produce.

Chongwe East Aspiring Parliamentary Candidate Sylvia Masebo highlighted the achievements recorded under the UPND administration, particularly through the implementation of Constituency Development Funds (CDF) projects.

Ms Masebo thanked President Hichilema for visiting Chongwe East Constituency and reaffirmed the party’s commitment to improving the welfare of residents.

The President also assured residents that the government will continue creating employment opportunities for young people through various economic empowerment and development programmes.

World.title: Muchinga ECZ staff undergo training
World.content:
Muchinga Province Electoral Officer Moffat Mwandila says the Electoral Commission of Zambia (ECZ) remains confident to deliver the August 13th general election, in a highly professional manner.

‎

‎Speaking when he officially opened Phase One of the ECZ training which has seen 130 ECZ Staff from Chinsali, Isoka, Nakonde and Mafinga districts taking part in the training, Mr Mwandila said ECZ depends on District Election Trainers (DETs) and other ECZ staff to transfer knowledge to frontline poll staff.

‎

‎Mr Mwandila said the quality of performance among the poll staff on election day depends on how well the officers will be trained.

‎

‎”A minor error during training can translate into a major error on poll day, therefore you must diligently guard the integrity of Electoral Commission of Zambia and the electoral process,” he said

‎

‎Mr Mwandila further urged all ECZ staff to execute duties with absolute unwavering political neutrality.

‎

‎Mr Mwandila has also cautioned the District Election Trainers and other ECZ staff to emphasise on impartiality and non-partisanship as they train election staff in their respective districts ahead of the August 13th General election.

‎

‎”I would like to emphasise that transparent and credible elections is only possible when every officer fully understands their role,” he said

‎

‎And speaking on the sidelines of the training, Chinsali District Election Trainer Matildah Chitina said the knowledge from the training will enable them to equip poll staff with the required information to deliver credible elections.

World.title: HH assures fostered development in Luangwa
World.content:
President Hakainde Hichilema has assured Luangwa residents in Feira Constituency of the government’s continued commitment to fostering development in the area.

President Hichilema says the massive development achieved in the district under his leadership is testament of the government’s fulfilment of its promises to the people of Luangwa since assuming office in 2021.

Speaking during a community engagement at Galamuka Grounds in Luangwa district, President Hichilema cited the construction of 103 housing units through Central Government funding, the construction of the first ever modern Kavuula market, the construction of Senior Chief Mburuma’s palace which is at over 95 percent completion rate and an irrigation scheme which is at 90 percent complete.

He said the next project is the construction of Chief Mphuka’s palace which is already in the pipeline.

He said the pontoon will assist the traders especially those trading in fish as the business has been helped to improve their livelihoods.

The President further explained that his government will ensure that a bridge between Zambia and Zimbabwe is constructed to foster economic development between the two countries.

“My administration will engage the Zimbabwean government so that we agree on the construction of Kanyemba Bridge which is of high importance for both countries,” he explained.

Mr Hichilema also assured the residents of Luangwa of youth employment at Chakwenga mine in the district that will be opened soon.

When addressing the network challenges faced in some parts of the district, President Hichilema pledged his commitment to ensuring that it is looked into.

“I have also been told about the challenges you people are facing due to human animal conflict which has affected your farming life. My administration will continue to provide the Food Reserve Agency (FRA) community maize sales until this challenge of animals is addressed,” he said.

President Hichilema also pledged the government’s obligation to ensure that the Kavalamanja R220 road that joins the D145 road is worked on.

He expressed happiness that Luangwa district is a beneficiary of the free education policy that was recently enacted into law, the recruitment of health workers and teachers, the increased Constituency Development Funds which now stands at K40 million, the Social Cash Transfer and the winter cropping programme.

The Head of State urged residents to re-elect him into power for the second term and vote for parliamentary, mayoral and local government candidates standing under the United Party for National Development (UPND) ticket in the general elections on August 13th , 2026.

He specifically requested the residents of Luangwa to support the Parliamentary candidate Danford Makayi, Mayoral Candidate Loveness Banda and Councillors in all the 17 wards of Feira Constituency.
